text:
The Mammoth beat Colorado 4-1 on Wednesday, ending a winless run that had stretched through six games, and they did it with an edge. Liam O'Brien scored first, and his line afterward, in the Denver Post via Corey Masisak, was "If you touch any of our top guys, me and the boys are coming for you." The teams meet outdoors in the Winter Classic, and the bad blood is already there.

That win was overdue. Utah is 11-9-3 with 25 points, and its play says it should have more. The Mammoth have 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 57% at five on five, contender numbers. They've also allowed 9.47 more goals than those chances usually produce, and by our count that's about four points left on the table. Karel Vejmelka was pulled Monday, two days after KSL Sports wrote that Utah needs more from him following a loss to San Jose; the crease is where the season has leaked.

The forwards are carrying it. Logan Cooley has 14 points in his last 10, though he also drew headlines for a punch on Vancouver's Linus Karlsson. Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton have 73% of the expected goals together. Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve, week to week (Daily Faceoff). Our playoff odds sit at 73%. André Tourigny's team is playing well enough; the goaltending just has to stop giving it back.
headline: Utah finally got paid for its play
